To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single lipid species can deliver multiple functions in eukaryotes by generating multiple pools of the lipid with distinct properties.

the repertoire of PI4,5P2 pools at diverse subcellular organelles is regulated by distinct lipid kinases, which generate functionally specialized pools of PI4, 5P2, and by mechanisms that control the diffusion of PI4, P5P2 at nanoscales.
PI(4, 5)P2 regulates multiple functions in diverse subcellular locations by a mechanism that includes regulation of the synthesis, metabolism, and diffusion of PI(4)P2 at the membrane level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the subcellular distribution of the lipid PI(4, 5)P2 and its impact on diverse subcellular functions.

understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the generation, diffusion and metabolism of PI(4)P and PI(4, 5)P2, and the functional consequences of these processes in the regulation of cell signalling, cell division and cell death.

elucidating the molecular basis of the specificity of PI4,5P2-mediated signalling at eukarya membranes and the molecular mechanisms that control the generation of functionally diverse PI4,5 P2 pools in diverse metazoans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single multi-functional phosphoinositide, PI(4, 5)P2, is a key player in the control of diverse subcelluar processes.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of PI(4.5)P2-mediated signalling are conserved across diverse eukaryotic species.

the molecular mechanisms that regulate the generation of functionally distinct PI(4)5P2 pools are conserved in eukaryotes and are shaped by a combination of molecular processes that control the availability of PI(4)P2 and its diffusion in the PM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PI(4, 5)P2 has been found to be a multi-functional lipid, which is involved in the regulation of diverse subcelluar processes in eukayotic cells.
PI(4, 5)P2 functions are regulated at multiple levels.
PI(4, 5)P2 has a unique role in the regulation of diverse subcelllar processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI(4, 5)P2 functions as a multi-functional signalling lipid that is regulated by mechanisms that are conserved across eukaryotes.
the diversity of PI(4.5)P2 functions is achieved by mechanisms that control its synthesis and availability at distinct subcellular sites.
PI(4, 5)P2 functions in eukaryotes are not limited to its well-established role at the PM.
